Coaches: every club has a coach with a style (possession, high press, counterattack, low block, direct play or balanced) and a quality. They get sacked for poor results and big clubs poach those who stand out.
  • Tactical fit: if you're a footballer, your attributes are compared with what your coach's style demands.
  • Market: buyer, seller, academy and balanced clubs; windows in summer (June to August) and in January. In ⚽ World football → Market you see transfers, values and each league's money.
  • Your club: buy it or found it from the Career menu or from ⚽ World football. You decide the wage bill, ticket prices, signings and who coaches.
  • Facilities: expand the stadium (with a building permit), build the training center and open an academy.
  • Licenses: with the right license you can coach your club yourself.

Every coach has an idea of how to play: possession, high press, counterattack, low block or direct play. Some styles neutralize others: a high press bothers possession teams but leaves space for the counterattack.
The clash of styles and the coach's quality shift each match's strength only a little. When the style changes, the squad takes a few months to adapt. Tap a club in any table to see its coach.
A player can shine under one coach and sit on the bench under another: every system demands different qualities.
Compare your attributes with those your coach's style values most. A good fit brings you closer to a starting spot; when a new coach arrives, his trust in you starts from zero.
Big clubs buy stars and sell dear; many clubs in Portugal, the Netherlands or South America live off selling players to the rich leagues; others bet on their academy.
The model decides how easily a club sells, at what price and who buys in each window. Academy clubs produce youth players with more potential.
In football a team's strength closely follows what it pays in wages: studies of the European leagues find that the wage bill explains most of a team's league position.
The wage bill places you in your league's spending table and the team's strength slowly moves toward what it pays for. Stars' wages count.
Leagues set requirements to compete: minimum stadium capacity, training facilities and finances in order.
The top division requires a training center. If your club finishes in a promotion spot without a license, the next club goes up; in the top division, the league fines you every season.
To coach in the professional leagues you need a license: in Europe the UEFA C, B, A and Pro, with courses lasting several months.
With the B you coach a regional club, with the A a second-division club and with the Pro a top-division club. Your strength as a coach rises every month you coach.
Big projects, like expanding a stadium, need a permit from the city council and can take time or be rejected.
The permit costs 1% of the work and takes 2 to 4 months; it's rejected 15% of the time. Only one project can run at a time.
